primary_region: Maharashtra — Solapur, Satara, Kolhapur, Sangli belts

Healthy.visual_symptoms: Uniform green leaves with glossy surface, thick firm stalks, no yellowing or lesions.
immediate_actions: Maintain regular drip/furrow irrigation
Apply scheduled fertilizer doses
Healthy.timeline: Healthy crop shows consistent growth of 2-3 cm/day during grand growth phase (June-October).

Red Rot.visual_symptoms: Sudden withering of top leaves. Internal stalk tissue turns red with white patches. Sour fermented smell when cut open. Leaves show reddening along midrib.
Red Rot.favourable_conditions: Warm humid weather 28-32°C, RH >80%, waterlogging. Most severe in ratoon crops during June-September.
Red Rot.severity_note: Most destructive sugarcane disease in Maharashtra. Can cause 100% loss in severely infected fields. Spreads rapidly through infected setts and waterways.
immediate_actions: Remove and destroy all infected stalks immediately — do NOT leave in field
Avoid waterlogging — improve drainage urgently
Drench soil with Carbendazim 0.1% around infection spots
Stop harvesting infected rows to prevent tool spread
Treat remaining seed setts with Carbendazim 0.1% for 15 minutes before planting
preventive_measures: Use only disease-free certified setts from reputed nurseries
Hot water treatment of setts at 50°C for 30 minutes before planting
Plant resistant varieties: CoM 0265, CoC 671
Avoid ratoon crop in infected fields for at least 2 seasons
Ensure good field drainage — ridge planting recommended
do_not: Irrigate infected fields through furrow — spreads pathogen
Use infected setts for next planting
Leave crop debris in field after harvest
watch_for: Rapid spread to adjacent rows within 7-10 days
Sour smell when stalks are cut
Red discolouration spreading upward through stalk
Red Rot.timeline: Once detected, remove infected material within 48 hours. New infections can appear for 3-4 weeks. Healthy plants typically unaffected if drainage improved.

Wilt.visual_symptoms: Yellowing and drying of top leaves (similar to drought stress). Internal stalk shows hollow cavity with purple-red discolouration. Roots may show decay.
Wilt.favourable_conditions: Soil moisture stress followed by heavy rain. Sandy soils. Late season (September-November).
Wilt.severity_note: Yield loss 30-60% in susceptible varieties. Often confused with drought stress.
immediate_actions: Apply irrigation immediately if soil dry
Apply Trichoderma viride 2 kg/acre as soil drench
Remove severely affected plants
preventive_measures: Maintain uniform soil moisture — drip irrigation preferred
Sett treatment with Bavistin 0.1% before planting
Use resistant varieties: Co 86032
Apply FYM and potash to improve root health
do_not: Allow prolonged drought followed by sudden heavy irrigation
Plant in poorly drained compacted soils
watch_for: Purple-red cavity in stalk when cut
Yellowing starting from top leaves and progressing downward
Wilt.timeline: Recovery possible in early stages with irrigation and bio-fungicide. Advanced cases cannot recover — focus on protecting adjacent rows.

Grassy Shoot.visual_symptoms: Profuse tillering producing thin, pale yellow grass-like shoots from base. Infected shoots shorter than normal, leaves narrow and light green-yellow.
Grassy Shoot.favourable_conditions: Leafhopper population surge in March-May and September-October. Warm dry conditions.
Grassy Shoot.severity_note: Once infected, stalk cannot be used for sugar or seed. Entire stool must be removed.
immediate_actions: Uproot and burn all infected stools immediately
Spray Monocrotophos 0.05% or Imidacloprid 0.05% to control leafhopper vector
Apply systemic insecticide granules (Carbofuran 3G) in soil around healthy plants
preventive_measures: Use disease-free certified planting material
Control leafhopper population before peak season
Avoid planting near infected ratoon or wild grass hosts
do_not: Use infected plants as seed setts
watch_for: Dense grass-like tillers at base of plant
Grassy Shoot.timeline: Remove infected stools within 1 week of detection. Monitor for new infections for 4-6 weeks.

Pokkah Boeng.visual_symptoms: Twisted, distorted, chlorotic young leaves at the growing point. Leaf blade fails to unfurl properly. In severe cases, top rotting with foul smell. Knife cut injury symptom on leaf blade.
Pokkah Boeng.favourable_conditions: Hot humid weather 25-35°C, RH >85%, frequent rain. Most common in June-September.
Pokkah Boeng.severity_note: Moderate yield loss if top shoot affected. Rarely kills the entire stalk.
immediate_actions: Spray Carbendazim 0.1% into the leaf whorl (boot leaf area)
Spray Mancozeb 0.25% as protective spray
Repeat every 10-14 days for 2 rounds
preventive_measures: Avoid excess nitrogen fertilization — promotes succulent growth
Plant tolerant varieties
Ensure good air circulation with appropriate row spacing
do_not: Apply excess urea during humid monsoon months
Neglect early symptoms — can lead to top rot
watch_for: Rotting of growing point (top rot stage — more serious)
Pokkah Boeng.timeline: Mild cases recover in 2-3 weeks. Top rot cases may lose the primary shoot but side shoots can compensate.

Ratoon Stunting.visual_symptoms: Reduced growth in ratoon crop compared to plant crop. Stalks thin, short. Leaves pale green. No dramatic visible symptoms — diagnosed by poor yield.
Ratoon Stunting.favourable_conditions: Spreads through infected setts and contaminated harvesting equipment. All growing conditions.
Ratoon Stunting.severity_note: Yield loss 10-30% in ratoon. Often not noticed until after one poor harvest season.
immediate_actions: Hot water treat all seed setts at 50°C for 30 minutes
Disinfect all harvesting tools with bleach solution between rows
Avoid ratoon after 2-3 ratoon cycles in same field
preventive_measures: Start from certified clean planting material
Maximum 2-3 ratoon cycles per field
Disinfect tools, machines between infected and clean fields
watch_for: Significantly lower ratoon yield compared to previous seasons
Gradual decline across multiple ratoon cycles
Ratoon Stunting.timeline: Spread is slow but cumulative. Replace with fresh clean planting material every 3-4 years.

Top Borer.visual_symptoms: Dead heart in young plants (central leaf dries, can be pulled out easily). In older plants: 'shot holes' on leaves, internodal boring causing hollow stalks.
immediate_actions: Apply Carbofuran 3G granules 8-10 kg/acre in whorl
Release Trichogramma chilonis egg parasitoid 50,000/acre × 5 releases at weekly intervals
Spray Chlorpyrifos 0.05% or Monocrotophos 0.05%
preventive_measures: Light trap monitoring — one trap per 5 acres
Destroy dried leaves and stubble after harvest
Avoid late planting
do_not: Ignore dead heart symptoms — early intervention critical

Pyrilla (Leafhopper).visual_symptoms: White waxy secretion on undersides of leaves. Yellowing of leaves. Sticky honeydew causing sooty mold. Insect jumps when plant is disturbed.
immediate_actions: Spray Malathion 50 EC 2ml/L or Dimethoate 30 EC 2ml/L
Release Epiricania melanoleuca parasitoid 5000-10000/acre
Avoid excess nitrogen which promotes dense foliage
do_not: Apply broad-spectrum insecticides that kill natural predators

fertilizer_schedule.basal: FYM 4 tons + Urea 25 kg + SSP 50 kg + MOP 25 kg at planting
fertilizer_schedule.grand_growth_phase: Urea 25 kg at 120 days if crop is thin

irrigation.drip_recommendation: Drip irrigation saves 40-50% water vs furrow. Preferred for Solapur belt.
